name: training-coverage experiment (x support extension) with data-volume control
registered: 2026-10-30, before any new demo was collected or any new model trained
question: Does extending expert demonstrations to box x in [0.34,0.38) m explain the boundary grasp failure (too-deep grasp -> box seated against palm -> 3-5 cm placement offset) of frozen C0/S1, and does it change the C0/S1 trade-off?

scope.architecture: ACT unchanged (ResNet18 scratch, dim 256, 2 enc layers, chunk 20, exec 20, no VAE)
scope.normalization: train-only statistics computed per dataset from its TRAIN episodes; floors unchanged (S1: state 0.02 rad, gripper 0.002 m; action floor off; C0: no floor); hyper-parameters unchanged
scope.baselines: frozen C0/S1 seeds 0,1,2 (checkpoints and x-sweep results untouched)
scope.no_deletion: existing datasets, checkpoints and logs are never modified

data.original: outputs/datasets/demo_train_clipped (60 demos, train region x [0.38,0.45], y [0.07,0.13], yaw [-0.20,0.20], base seed 10, light jitter 0.15)

new_extension.name: demo_ext
new_extension.note: x uniform in [0.34,0.38) (upper end open); same expert, cameras (front, wrist_left, wrist_right), 120x160, 20 Hz, fast render profile; only demos with plan_ok and task_success are kept

new_volume_control.name: demo_vol
new_volume_control.note: same procedure and count as the extension but drawn from the ORIGINAL training region: adds data volume without adding coverage

merged.EXT: 60 original + demo_ext (original episodes first, identical order/content)

split.rule: original 60 keep their V1 split (54 train / 6 val, outputs/lerobot/pickplace_v1/openarm_splits.json); of each 30 new demos 27 go to train and 3 to val (val chosen with numpy default_rng(0) over the sorted new episode indices)
split.note: the 3 new val demos only monitor validation loss; no test seeds involved

data.sizing_rationale: original density 60 demos over a 0.07 m x-range ~ 0.86/cm; 30 demos over 0.04 m = 0.75/cm (similar). If fewer than 30 extension demos succeed, VOL is sized to the same kept count.

training.seed_note: 3 and 4 are new independent seeds (baselines used 0,1,2); EXT arms are paired by seed id (same init and batch order for the same dataset); VOL has one seed per arm
training.compute_budget: identical 5400 steps for every branch (fixed compute); steps per demo therefore fall by 1/1.5 for the 90-demo datasets - a known confound shared by EXT and VOL, separated from coverage only by the VOL control
training.guard: average of the first 200 steps <= 1.10 s/step else stop and report

xsweep.note: the existing frozen x-sweep is rerun verbatim on each new checkpoint (60 poses: 15 x x 4 blocks)

shortcut.set: NOM seed 21 ids 0-19 (training region, as in E0): unperturbed, right_mean, right_jitter_small
shortcut.SI: success perturbed / success unperturbed on the same ids

evaluation.open_loop_val: MAE on the 6 ORIGINAL validation episodes of pickplace_v1 (comparable with baselines)
evaluation.latency: per-step and per-query inference latency from the evaluation logs (cpu, 1 thread); hardware-noise caveat
evaluation.replay: eval/xsweep_replay.py on every sweep rollout for offsets and contacts
metrics: task success by x and stratum
grasp offset a_close (TCP frame) and deviation from expert
evaluation.note: for the EXT branches x in [0.34,0.38) is now IN training support; strata keep their old names for comparability

uncertainty.across_training_seeds: per-seed values, range and sign consistency (EXT n=2 per arm, baseline n=3, VOL n=1); t-intervals with df<=2 are shown only for reference
uncertainty.across_pose_blocks: block-resampling bootstrap within seed and per-block tables (4 blocks); the block factor is crossed with x
uncertainty.caveat: EXT/VOL vs baseline comparisons are between independent training seeds (not paired)

hypotheses.C1: Coverage improves boundary success: for BOTH arms, mean EXT success over x in [0.34,0.37] >= baseline same-arm mean + 20 pp AND >= 75 %, AND each EXT seed >= baseline mean + 10 pp.
hypotheses.C2: Volume control: for BOTH arms the VOL (seed 3) success over x in [0.34,0.37] <= baseline same-arm mean + 10 pp (=> improvement is attributable to coverage, not data volume). If VOL >= baseline + 20 pp the volume confound is evident.
hypotheses.C3: Grasp position: for BOTH arms mean |a_close - a_close(expert)| over x in [0.34,0.37] <= 1.0 cm in every EXT seed AND improved by >= 1.5 cm vs the baseline same-arm mean deviation.
hypotheses.C4: Trade-off: S1 - C0 over x in [0.34,0.37], paired by EXT seed (3,4): mean >= -10 pp => the S1 boundary deficit is explained by coverage; also report S1-C0 over x in [0.38,0.45] (NON-INFERIOR if the lower t-bound >= -10 pp, which is unreachable with df=1; verdict then INCONCLUSIVE unless COST EVIDENT).
hypotheses.C5: No in-support regression: for BOTH arms EXT success over x in [0.38,0.45] >= baseline same-arm mean - 10 pp.
hypotheses.C6: Shortcut sensitivity retained: S1-EXT SI >= 0.90 on right_mean and jitter_small in every seed; C0-EXT SI <= 0.25 in every seed.
hypotheses.C7: Coverage effect is local: for BOTH arms |EXT - baseline same-arm mean| <= 15 pp over x in [0.46,0.48].
hypotheses.C8: Latency (descriptive): median per-query latency of new checkpoints within +-25 % of the frozen baselines.
hypotheses.overall_rule: COVERAGE EXPLAINS the boundary grasp failure if C1 and C2 and C3 hold; PARTIAL if C1 holds but C2 or C3 fails (volume confound or only partial grasp-position recovery); NOT EXPLAINED if C1 fails. C4-C8 qualify the conclusion and the S1/C0 trade-off. All other analyses are exploratory.

acceptance.AC1: new demos: >= 27/30 expert successes (plan_ok and task_success) for both EXT and VOL; kept counts reported
acceptance.AC2: dataset synchronization validation passes (data/validate_dataset.py on the new raw sets; data/validate_merge.py: frame counts, timestamps, state/action alignment, first 60 episodes bit-identical to the V1 LeRobot dataset, split manifest, train-only stats recomputed)
acceptance.AC3: unit tests (policies/test_norm_contract.py) pass and a 200-step smoke training on the EXT dataset for both arms completes with norm contracts verified (floors only on live idle right-arm dims for S1)
acceptance.AC4: all 6 training runs reach 5400 steps with the speed guard satisfied
acceptance.AC5: every checkpoint completes the 60-pose sweep, the 3 x 20 shortcut episodes and the open-loop check
acceptance.AC6: no forbidden seed; this config's sha256 unchanged; baselines untouched (hashes re-checked)

budget.stop_rules: stop and report if the first-200-step speed guard trips, if projected total > 14 h, if a run crashes twice with identical arguments, or if a forbidden seed appears
